name: Learn basic wrestling and grappling movements
blurb: Stance, level change, sprawl, shrimping and bridging — the movements that make up the vocabulary of every grappling art, and all of them trainable solo.
gear: Ideally a training partner, or a class
steps: Learn the athletic stance: knees bent, back straight, head up, hands ready.
Learn the level change — dropping the hips rather than bending at the waist — which underpins every takedown.
Drill the penetration step for a double-leg takedown, slowly, on air or a dummy.
Learn the sprawl as the counter: hips down and back, legs shot behind you, weight on the opponent.
Learn shrimping and bridging on the ground — the two escapes that everything defensive is built from.
Find a class. Grappling above the solo-drill level genuinely requires a partner and supervision.
tips: Bending at the waist instead of the knees is the fault that makes beginners easy to take down.
Solo drills build movement quality, but real grappling needs a resisting partner and a coach.
proof: You flow through stance, level change, penetration step, sprawl, shrimp and bridge without pausing to think.
